site.sight:arena1: Six living oaks stand round a floor of mossy stone. A stone sits on a dais in the middle.
site.sight:arena2: Loose sand fills a bowl inside a gilded rim, with a stone on a gilded dais.
site.sight:arena3: Eight pillars of stacked bone, capped with azure crystal, ring a pad of dressed stone.
site.sight:arena4: Under a dome of fungus, four lamps hang over a stone.
site.sight:arena5: Tall masts stand round a stone, brick at the foot and glassed stone toward the top.
site.sight:arena6: Ringed in crystal, a disc of rock lies in open air. Single stones run off it and stop.
site.sight:arena7: Ten pillars of black glass, capped with violet crystal, stand round a stone in the open.
site.sight:arena8: Lanterns on eight stepped heaps ring a raised base of dressed stone with a stone on top.
site.sight:burned_hearths: The floor round the hearthstone is burned black. The rest of the house is whole.
site.sight:cache1: Square walls of dressed stone stand in the cavern, open at one narrow doorway.
site.sight:cache2: A small disc of turf hangs in open air with a chest on it and nothing leading to it.
site.sight:column: From the summit a column of rubble one piece wide goes straight up and stops in the air.
site.sight:crossing: Single dressed stones stand in the water in a line out from the shore.
site.sight:dungeon: Rooms of dressed stone, joined by passages. No stair or shaft leads up out of them.
site.sight:fire_ring: A fire burns on a floor of black glass. Low houses ring it, every door facing in.
site.sight:fold: Two short walls of rubble meet in a corner, with an oak standing in the angle.
site.sight:hearth: Set into the floor opposite the door is a block of dressed stone.
site.sight:lamp_row: Three fungus lamps hang in a straight line, evenly spaced, under the roof.
site.sight:lone_tree: One tree stands alone with leaves that give light, and no other tree near it.
site.sight:pan: In the shore sandstone a square is cut one piece deep, inside a raised rim.
site.sight:prints: Prints run across the snow in a short line. Clean snow lies at both ends.
site.sight:quarry: The slope has a square bite cut out of it, with flat faces and one half-dressed block.
site.sight:ruin: Stone walls with clean gaps in them stand round a paved floor and a lamp on a pillar.
site.sight:shaft: Walled in dressed stone, a square shaft goes straight down out of sight.
site.sight:stump: Among the standing spires are stumps of crystal one piece high.
site.sight:tree_floor: High among the trunks is a floor of planks with a lamp on it, and no way up.
site.sight:village: Houses stand in a ring round a lit well, every door facing it.
codex.seen:place:0: Sound ground in every direction, as far as any of us has walked. A sun, a moon, and stars that turn. Old stonework stands in every country, and most of it is empty.
codex.read:place:0: Our own grounds are thinning. This one is sound wherever we go, and what is set here stays set. It seems to lie on dead wood, which holds steady whatever lies over it.
codex.born:place:0: This is the ground, peopl, and there is no other. The forebears raised the stones on it and built to the ends of it. It has always been sound.
codex.seen:place:1: No sky. Caverns open into caverns, lit by fungus and crystal, with rock and standing water between. Feeders are up here at every hour. A bed laid here marks nothing.
codex.read:place:1: Dug down, the floor here is the same black face as the floor above, and the roof is the same again. So the hollow is inside the wood, between two faces of it. Nothing we carry cuts that wood.
codex.born:place:1: Under is where the things of the night come from. Nobody holds a hearth down there. I will not go through your gate, peopl, and no householder will.
codex.seen:place:2: Islands in two layers in open air, with nothing between them and nothing below. The sun stands just under the edge and the stars do not turn. Pale sheets hang under the lower layer.
codex.read:place:2: A step off an edge ends back on the last footing, hurt. The hour does not move. The order of things is broken here, as it is in the hollow. The remains that open the gate point up, so we take these to be overhead.
codex.seen:country:ocean: Open water at one height, as far as anyone can see. The floor is sand, with clay in the shallows and gravel further out. Fish swim in it. No feeder has been met in it at any hour.
codex.read:country:ocean: A feeder takes its body from what it feeds on, and water has nothing set in it. That would be why nothing comes up in the sea. The lines of single stones show that people once crossed it on foot.
codex.seen:country:beach: Sand over sandstone at the edge of the water, with reeds where the grass begins. No creature lives on the open shore. By day there is nothing in the water on one side and no cover on the other.
codex.read:country:beach: The sea works the edge of the land loose, and loose ground that lies long enough sets again, which is what the sandstone is. The square pans cut in it are where salt was dried.
codex.seen:country:plains: Open grass with a lone oak here and there. Sheep graze it in small flocks and grouse run in the long grass. Kinva sit in the grass by day.
codex.read:country:plains: Nothing is tilled anywhere on this ground. Flocks gone wild keep this grass open. The fold corners mean it was cleared for flocks once, and they were shut in at night.
codex.seen:country:palewood: Pale-barked trees make a light wood, with grass, flowers and berry bushes under them and a few young oaks coming up between. Sheep and grouse. Kantak stand among the bushes by day.
codex.read:country:palewood: The pale tree is the first to seed into open ground, and oak comes up under it later. The flowers of pasture are still on the floor. This was pasture, then, given up some time back.
codex.seen:country:forest: Old oak wood, with fern, brown mushroom and berry bushes under it and a pale tree here and there. Apples fall from the oaks. Sheep, grouse and boar. Kantak and Kinva are out by day.
codex.read:country:forest: Where a village stands under the oaks, that ground was cleared and lived on, and the wood came back over it. Elsewhere the trees do not show whether it was ever cleared at all.
codex.seen:country:bloomvale: Short pale turf thick with flowers, and trees in blossom. White and blue flowers outnumber the red. The turf is paler and bluer than the grass of the country round it.
codex.read:country:bloomvale: The white and blue flowers and the pale turf are the growth of the islands. Seed must have come back through gates on feet and loads, and taken here, and gone on spreading.
codex.seen:country:swamp: Mud at the height of the sea, broad low oaks, reeds and mushrooms, and a haze that does not lift. Kaddam lie sunk in the mud with the head showing, and stand when a body comes near.
codex.read:country:swamp: A Lees Lump is lees set hard in mud, and a Kaddam swallows it with the mud. Whatever dies in the mire sinks where nothing renders it. Its lees lies in the mud and sets, as it does in rock.
codex.seen:country:taiga: Cold pine wood with fern, and more berry bushes than any other country. Snow lies on its higher ground. Boar root here by day. At night Vaka run in ones to threes.
codex.read:country:taiga: There is too little green growth among the pines for the day kinds, so nothing hostile is out here by day. Its pine villages are stocked like the rest, and householders pass through them.
codex.seen:country:tundra: Flat snow over grass, a pine or a dry bramble here and there, and ice along the sea. No village. By day nothing hostile walks it, and a stone or a store shows from a long way off.
codex.read:country:tundra: It has no timber, no fuel and no flock, so nobody raised a house here. On snow a feeder can be seen to come up out of nothing: its prints start in clean snow with no trail behind them.
codex.seen:country:desert: Sand over deep sandstone, with cactus and dry bramble. Hares run on it by day. Angār come up over the sand at night. Villages of sandstone stand round wells.
codex.read:country:desert: Sand is rock with the firmness eaten out of it, which would be the work of the sand kinds. A hard fire kept on sand long enough runs it to glass, and the sand-country people live round such fires.
codex.seen:country:savanna: Tall dry grass with low flat-topped kapok trees standing far apart. Sheep and hares. Kinva by day, and Angār over the grass at night. Villages stand in it.
codex.read:country:savanna: The kapok is the tree of the hot wet wood, standing thin. This is the nearest timber to the sand, and it has been cut for fuel. Householders and the sand-country people both use its villages.
codex.seen:country:jungle: Hot wet wood, the tallest trees on the ground, over fern. Grouse are the only animal in it. Kantak stand in the undergrowth. There is no village anywhere in it.
codex.read:country:jungle: No flock lives here, so no hearth could be fed and no village was built. The plank floors high in the trunks are where people slept who came to work the stones.
codex.seen:country:crags: High stone, with grass on the flats, bare rock on the slopes and a few pines. Coal and iron show in the cliff faces without digging. Jatu hang under the overhangs at night.
codex.read:country:crags: Hard rock lies at the surface here. The squared cuts in the slopes are quarries, and the half-dressed blocks in them mean hard stone for housings was cut here, and the cutting stopped.
codex.seen:country:peaks: Snow over stone above everything else, and nothing growing. Coal shows in the faces. Vaka and Jatu are out on it at night.
codex.read:country:peaks: Height alone makes this country. The tall columns on its summits are the only work of people here, and a bedroll at the foot of one means whoever stacked it had a way.
codex.seen:country:hollows: Caverns floored with fungal turf, set with glowing fronds and mushrooms, and fungus stems as tall as trees where the roof is high. Antar ore runs through the rock.
codex.read:country:hollows: Fungus grows on everything that dies down here, since nothing is boiled down or burned. Growth scatters. A straight row of lamps was hung by a person, so people came this way.
codex.seen:country:hollows_crystal: Bare hollow rock with spires of azure and violet crystal, some taller than a person, and almost no fungus. The crystal lights the floor round it. Tala ore lies in the lower rock.
codex.read:country:hollows_crystal: Standing crystal is lees that nothing ate, and its colour follows the kind it came from. Something fed here on a great many of a violet kind and left what it did not finish.
codex.seen:country:rift: Turf over soil over island rock. Trees with lit leaves, grass, and white and blue flowers. Pale sheets hang under the edges. Vihanga and Kajjot are in the air.
codex.read:country:rift: The fruit on these trees neither ripens nor rots. Nothing here has gone through a day since the sky stopped, it seems. This is the surface of some ground as it stood at that dusk.
codex.seen:country:rift_shards: Islands set with spires of pale crystal, with white flowers between and no trees. Sakal stand among the spires and do not move until something comes near.
codex.read:country:rift_shards: Some spires are eaten down to stumps. Sakal feed on the crystal, so this is their pasture. The crystal is the oldest we have found and has set harder than any other.
codex.seen:site:village: Four to six houses round a well, every door facing it, one lamp over the well. Each house has a crate, a lamp, and a bedroll or a workbench. The crates are stocked. Nobody lives in them.
codex.read:site:village: The bedrolls in these houses work for us, and no born person has a use for one. Householders stock the crates and pass a night here. So people with a way once lived in these houses beside people without one.
codex.born:site:village: The forebears built these and lived in them. A hearth went dark when nobody was left to sit at it. We pass nights in them now, and fill the crates for whoever comes next.
codex.seen:site:ruin: Walls up to four high stand round a paved floor nine strides square, with clean gaps broken in them. A lamp on a pillar, a chest. None of the stone is dressed. Some have a nest under the floor.
codex.read:site:ruin: Its chest still held gear and some lees, so whoever broke the walls did not empty it. It is a store built on top of the ground, by people who did not cut down into the rock as the sealed stores were.
codex.born:site:ruin: Feeders broke into those, and the sand-country people. The forebears stored on top of the ground when they could no longer go under it. Look in the chest, peopl.
codex.sand:site:ruin: We broke some of those and burned what was in them. What is stored draws.
codex.seen:site:dungeon: Three to five rooms of dressed stone joined by passages, deep under solid rock, with no way in from above. Pillars carry lamps or azure crystal. Most rooms hold a nest, and the last holds the chest.
codex.read:site:dungeon: Gear, lees, a bait made ahead and a stone for the way, all in one chest. This was a working store for hunters who could live where feeders are up at every hour. Only one of us can use that stone.
codex.born:site:dungeon: Any of us who digs down to a sealed store does not come up. Bring a tool out of one whole, peopl. I want to see how the forebears worked.
codex.sand:site:dungeon: The stores under the rock are full because nobody went back for them. Empty one in the sand country before a march finds it, and nobody has to die breaking it.
codex.seen:site:cache1: Dressed stone, one room seven strides square, with a doorway one piece wide. Inside are two fungus lamps, a chest, and a nest of Asikavak.
codex.read:site:cache1: It is the same dressed stone as the sealed stores above. Whoever built those crossed into the hollow too, and left a smoker for the Guhamāt ready in the chest.
codex.seen:site:cache2: Between the two layers hangs a disc of turf and island rock, with a chest and two posts of island timber capped with crystal. Nothing that walks reaches it.
codex.read:site:cache2: An island has no depth of rock to seal a room under, so this store is sealed by air. It holds a bait ready, as the vaults below do. People crossed to these islands and stored here.
codex.seen:site:arena1: Six living oaks are the posts of a paved round of mossy stone, with glowing mushrooms in a ring. The stone sits on a dais of mossy brick.
codex.read:site:arena1: When the Vanahar came up its roots went into the joints of the paving and up the oaks. The mushrooms grow where carcasses were boiled down for a long time. Kills were boiled here, often.
codex.born:site:arena1: That is the Vanahar Altar. The forebears set the Vanahar over the woods when they raised it. One stands a short walk from where peopls come up.
codex.sand:site:arena1: Every stone feeds what lies at it. That one lies nearest the place peopls come up out of the ground.
codex.seen:site:arena2: A bowl sunk three deep and filled with loose sand, rimmed in gilded brick, with four pillars on the rim and the stone on a gilded dais in the sand.
codex.read:site:arena2: The Maruhar came up through the sand. The sand was carried here and the bowl dug for it. The rim is faced with gold, which a stone-eater cannot eat, since the animal would lie against it.
codex.born:site:arena2: The Maruhar Altar. Stand on the rim, peopl. The sand in the bowl is where it comes up.
codex.sand:site:arena2: Our burrower lay at these. It was the price of the sand, and it let nothing else in. Leave that stone bare and another will come onto the empty sand.
codex.seen:site:arena3: Eight pillars of stacked bone, each capped with azure crystal, stand on a pad of dressed stone and stone brick. At the foot of every second pillar a cell of the paving is crystal.
codex.read:site:arena3: The pillars are the bone that is left in the pot when a carcass is boiled down, stacked up. The caps are lees that spilled and set. Many Tama were boiled down on this floor.
codex.seen:site:arena4: A dome cut in hollow rock, floored with fungal turf and lined inside with fungus cap. Six fungus stems with wide caps stand round the stone, and four fungus lamps hang under the roof.
codex.read:site:arena4: When the smoke reached the roof, the roof moved. The dome is the Guhamāt's own growth, and it hangs by it. Nobody could hold a stone where no dawn comes, so this one was only ever baited.
codex.seen:site:arena5: Six tall masts stand round the stone on a pad of stone brick. Each is brick at the foot and turns to glassed stone toward the top.
codex.read:site:arena5: The masts are for flying a kite. The Jīmūt never landed. The glassed stone is brick its throws loosened, set again, thickest high up where it circled.
codex.seen:site:arena6: Island rock five thick, flecked with crystal, laid as a disc in open air, with eight crystal pillars. A line of single stones runs out from the rim and stops.
codex.read:site:arena6: Set ground stays where it is laid, so whoever built this laid a floor in the air and the way out to it a stone at a time. The crystal is lees spilled when kills were boiled on it.
codex.seen:site:arena7: Black glass and deep rock pave this floor under the open sky. Ten pillars of black glass stand on it, capped with violet crystal.
codex.read:site:arena7: The Kuranga comes only at night. Black glass and deep rock were carried up from far below to make this floor. The violet caps are the lees of its kind, set, so that kind was killed here before.
codex.born:site:arena7: The Kuranga Altar. Wear the mask at it after dark, peopl, and it comes up to see who wears it. It never comes under the sun.
codex.seen:site:arena8: A raised base of dressed stone in three tiers, with the stone on top, ringed by eight stepped heaps that each carry a lantern.
codex.read:site:arena8: The Nihān came up through the base, which is hollowed from beneath. It held arms better than any other store we have opened. So the base was a store, and the Nihān ate into it.
codex.born:site:arena8: The Cairn. When the great lees ran out, the forebears closed their first and best stone under it, to save it for the day it can be lit again.
codex.sand:site:arena8: They closed that heap over a thing nobody could kill and set lamps round it. The stones fattened it like the others.
codex.seen:site:burned_hearths: In some houses here the floor round every hearthstone is burned black. The crates are stocked like any others. Nothing in the houses says who did it.
codex.born:site:burned_hearths: The sand-country people did that on a march. They burn whatever they cannot carry home.
codex.sand:site:burned_hearths: The people of those houses burned their own floors on the day they walked out.
codex.seen:site:fire_ring: One fire burns day and night on a round floor of black glass. Six to ten sandstone houses ring it, doors to the fire, and fuel is stacked inside the ring. No chest, pot or bed.
codex.read:site:fire_ring: Broken out, the floor is sand run to glass with ash through it, from a fire that burned kills on it for generations. A token comes out of it, so every token is a piece of some fire's floor.
codex.born:site:fire_ring: Their fires want more wood than the sand will ever grow. They have nothing I want. I carry nothing to them.
codex.sand:site:fire_ring: Inside the light is the only safe ground we have now. Whoever has the fuel says who sleeps there.
codex.seen:site:hearth: Set into the floor of every old house, against the wall opposite the door, is a slab of dressed stone. It is the stone a householder sits at.
codex.read:site:hearth: Under a few of these lay a ward core. Householders hold at the same stones without one. Whoever set those cores built as wards are built where a core is needed.
codex.born:site:hearth: A hearthstone carries what the hand drives down into the pot. The forebears set one in every house. I cut the slabs householders carry on the road.
codex.seen:site:column: A column of rubble one piece wide stands far above a summit and ends in nothing. A bedroll lies at its foot, and a torch on the other side.
codex.read:site:column: The bedroll means whoever stacked it had a way, as we do. No born person thinks there is anything overhead. One of us tried to build up to the islands and stopped.
codex.seen:site:crossing: Single dressed stones set at the waterline, open water between each, in a line out from the shore. A second stone stands on top of the last stone in the line.
codex.read:site:crossing: A stone set at the waterline stays with nothing under it, and nothing comes up in water. Someone walked out over the sea a stone at a time. The stone carried out and never set is where the work stopped.
codex.seen:site:fold: Two runs of rubble two high meet at a right angle, with an oak standing in the angle.
codex.read:site:fold: It is the corner of a fold where flocks were shut in at night, it seems, with one oak left for shade. The rest of the wall was carried off for other work.
codex.seen:site:lamp_row: Three fungus lamps hang in a straight row under the roof, evenly spaced.
codex.read:site:lamp_row: Growth down here scatters. A row this straight was hung by a person, and it points at a vault or a stone.
codex.seen:site:lone_tree: Alone among the flowers stands a tree with a pale trunk and leaves that give light. Nothing comes up under it. Now and then its leaves drop a fruit.
codex.read:site:lone_tree: Its fruit is Island Fruit, and the white and blue flowers round it grow on the islands too. Seed came down from there, it seems, on whoever crossed back.
codex.seen:site:pan: A square pan cut one piece deep in the shore sandstone, inside a rim. Most are full of blown sand. A few near villages are clean, with a white crust on the floor.
codex.read:site:pan: Sea water left in a cut like this dries in the sun to salt, with no fuel spent. Every charge is packed in salt. The clean pans lie near villages, where a householder still needs it.
codex.seen:site:prints: Prints in clean snow, in a short line. Nothing stands at either end, and no trail leads to the first print.
codex.read:site:prints: Elsewhere a feeder is found where nothing was, and nobody sees it come. Here the snow shows the place it came up.
codex.seen:site:quarry: Cut into the slope is a square bite with flat faces and a floor of stone. One half-dressed block stands at the foot.
codex.read:site:quarry: Ground here comes away in whole pieces, so a quarry is a squared cut. The block was being dressed for something, and nobody came back to finish it.
codex.seen:site:shaft: A square shaft walled in dressed stone from the turf to the floor. The walls shut out caves, water and molten rock all the way down. A chest stands at the bottom.
codex.read:site:shaft: It passes every seam of ore without a side cut. It was sunk to reach the floor and nothing else, and the saw left at the bottom was made for root-wood.
codex.seen:site:stump: Among whole spires of pale crystal stand others eaten down to stumps one piece high.
codex.read:site:stump: The island kinds feed on crystal. These spires are their pasture, and the stumps are where Sakal have been at them.
codex.seen:site:tree_floor: Kapok planks make a floor high among the trunks, with a lamp, a crate and a bedroll on it. Nothing leads up to it.
codex.read:site:tree_floor: No village was built in this country, since nothing grazes to feed a hearth. Whoever worked the stones here slept off the ground, and took the steps up behind them.
codex.seen:material:wood: Timber of the living ground. Bare hands take it, and it splits to planks by hand.
codex.read:material:wood: A wooden pick breaks stone and nothing softer does. Hardness here goes in steps, it seems, each taken by the step before it.
codex.seen:material:stone: The common rock under the soil. A pick brings it away as rubble, and fire closes rubble back to stone.
codex.read:material:stone: A stone pick takes the rock iron lies in. Dressed stone in the old houses needs a stone pick where raw stone takes a wooden one, so stone that lies long dressed has set harder.
codex.seen:material:iron: Ordinary iron from the upper and middle rock. A wood fire melts it to bars. It also comes out of old chests, and out of the Nihirakka that nest among stored iron.
codex.read:material:iron: Hīrak comes away whole under an iron pick, where a stone pick breaks it to nothing. Iron is the last metal a wood fire moves. Everything harder lies deeper, nearer the floor.
codex.seen:material:lumenite: Rare, clear, and giving a cold light, this gem lies low in the living ground. It comes away whole under an iron pick and is cleaved on the anvil's edge. No fire moves it.
codex.read:material:lumenite: A Hīrak pick takes the black glass and the warm ore beside the molten rock. Lees that lies uneaten sets to crystal. This is clearer and harder and lies deeper, so it may be lees set further still.
codex.born:material:lumenite: It is crystal that went past use. A hand drives nothing through it. Kammār calls it a stone because it takes an edge. There is a piece of it in every recall stone I cut.
codex.seen:material:cinder: Iron ore from the lowest rock but one, beside the molten rock, still warm when cut. A furnace does not move it. It runs only in the bed of a Maruhar Furnace.
codex.read:material:cinder: The ore of the hollow yields to a Jalit pick. This is iron that ran with the molten rock and set again all at once, deep and near the floor: iron, it seems, at a second hardness.
codex.born:material:cinder: No fire of mine moves that ore. I shape the bars you bring out of the Maruhar Furnace, and that is as far as my trade goes with it.
codex.seen:material:umbrite: The metal of the hollow's rock, found at every height there. The bed of a Maruhar Furnace that runs Jalit runs this as well.
codex.read:material:umbrite: Its pick takes the lower ore of the hollow. The hollow lies between two faces of the floor, and this metal is set harder than anything above the lowest rock of the living ground.
codex.born:material:umbrite: I know it only as bars peopls bring up from Under. I have never seen its ore. Bring me a piece raw, if you can carry it.
codex.seen:material:noctrium: The same metal as Antar, from the lower half of the hollow down to the standing water. The Maruhar bed leaves it as it was. A Guhamāt Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:noctrium: Island ore yields to a Tala pick. The lower metal of the hollow lies nearer its floor and is set harder for it, which fits hardness coming from the floor.
codex.seen:material:aether: The common metal of the islands, in more veins than iron has below. It is cut over drops that do not land. A Guhamāt Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:aether: An Ākās pick takes the island seams that have crystal through them. If hardness is age, the islands are older than anything on the living ground above its floor.
codex.seen:material:prism: Seams of the islands' metal with pale crystal grown through it. The crystal does not split and the metal does not bend. Only a Ratan Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:prism: Nothing made of the living ground's own matter cuts its lowest rock. A Patik pick does, so working our own floor wanted both gates.
codex.seen:material:eclipse: Ore from the lowest rock, lying on the floor itself, a single vein in a wide stretch. It gives a violet light. Only a Kuranga Furnace runs it.
codex.read:material:eclipse: It is iron set as hard as anything sets here, lying on the floor with lees through it. Its light is the colour of the things of the dark night, and some of us say they are made of it.
codex.seen:matter:gold: Soft metal from the deep rock. A wood fire melts it and the hammer never hardens it. It holds no edge.
codex.read:matter:gold: The Maruhar bowls are rimmed in gold, and a gold bar weights its lure. Its kind eats stone and gets nothing from gold. Gold, then, is what stone is faced with where a stone-eater will lie.
codex.seen:matter:lees: Feeders boiled down overnight leave a dark residue, which is packed in salt. Every householder takes it, weighed out, for anything. Feeders yield it at the kill.
codex.read:matter:lees: A sheep pays nothing, because lees is what is left of a feeder's body and a sheep is no feeder. Every hearth uses some each night, which is why every householder takes it.
codex.born:matter:lees: Every hearth on the road uses a pot of it a night, and most are short. Weigh it into my hand and I will carry it where it is wanted.
codex.sand:matter:lees: Lees is what the dark comes up for. We burn every kill so there is none. What a march takes from your chests goes into the fire.
codex.seen:matter:crystal: Lees set hard. Driven along cut lines it loosens what it is pointed at, and does nothing else. Shut in rock it forms geodes. In the open it stands and gives light.
codex.read:matter:crystal: Crystal is lees that nothing found. The jar-shaped crystal from an old store shows it. The standing crystal of the caverns is the same lees, set in the open where it had room to grow.
codex.born:matter:crystal: Crystal grows in dark rock. There is no kill in it. I cut the lines to it and the arm does the rest.
codex.sand:matter:crystal: Crystal is lees gone hard. The Dāhaga take it out of the stores for the fire, with the rest.
codex.seen:matter:salt: A white crust on the floor of a square pan cut in the shore sandstone. It breaks to nothing in the hand.
codex.read:matter:salt: A nest is a store where the salt failed. Unsalted lees is food, and feeders came to it and bred. Every charge is packed in salt for that reason, and the pans on the shore are where it was dried.
codex.seen:matter:remains: Parts as they come off a feeder: flesh, sac, dust, shard, scale. Raw, they are food to feeders. They go into baits and onto carved bone.
codex.read:matter:remains: A small feeder formed on the carved bone and stayed by the hand that carried it. Raw remains are food. It stays for the food, it seems, and for nothing else.
codex.born:matter:remains: What is on the bone feeds it, and it stays for that. Raw is food to all of them. Carry it salted, or carry it well away from my pot.
codex.sand:matter:remains: Raw is food, and food draws. We burn it before dark. A peopl who feeds a small one by hand is carrying what draws.
codex.seen:matter:great_remains: Raw remains of the strongest of a host. They still move, and they go on loosening whatever is near them. One piece goes into each furnace, bench or gate.
codex.read:matter:great_remains: Fire wakes the remains in the ring, and they loosen ore that no fire moves. A furnace like that is a store of great remains with no hand on it. It draws, as a spent charge does.
codex.born:matter:great_remains: The fresh remains of the Vanahar loosen made things. An old holder's hand sets like metal. I want to know whether they will loosen that too.
codex.sand:matter:great_remains: Every piece you build into a furnace or a gate draws, day and night. We would burn all of it.
codex.seen:people:householders: Born people who hold a house ward: a clay pot of lees and one hand on a slab of cut stone until dawn. Each has a trade for the day. Few have a house. They walk by day between the old houses.
codex.read:people:householders: None of them will go to a great stone or through a gate. They die where they are killed and have no way, it seems, which is why the hunting falls to us and the holding to them.
codex.sand:people:householders: They sit beside pots and call it holding. Their pots are what the dark comes up for, and they send peopls to the stones to fill them.
codex.seen:people:sand: Born people of the sand who hold no pot and burn every kill. They live round fires on black glass. Their fighters march on the houses at dawn and turn for home at dusk.
codex.read:people:sand: A token is glass from under one of their fires, with ash through it. They burn kills hot enough to run sand to glass, which would leave nothing to boil down and nothing to draw.
codex.born:people:sand: They gave up the pot and burn what they kill. They break stores and burn what is in them. The Deserter sits at a pot now, and holds it badly.
codex.read:people:peopls: Each of us came up alone with nothing, long apart from the rest. A company in the road is taken, and so is anyone carrying a load. Only those who drop everything and walk on come up, it seems.
codex.born:people:peopls: A peopl comes up at the mouth with nothing in its hands and gets up again after a killing. The ground puts you out there. You were never born anywhere.
codex.sand:people:peopls: Peopls come up out of the ground with nothing and go to the old stores. Kill one and nobody sees it go, and in the morning another is there. A host does the same at its stones.
codex.seen:old:cutter_saw: Two-handled, steel, from the bottom of a shaft sunk to the floor. Its middle teeth are stripped and the teeth at either end are whole.
codex.read:old:cutter_saw: It goes through standing timber faster than any axe made here. It is a saw for cutting broken root-wood. Whoever carried it down the shaft tried it on the floor, and the floor stripped it.
codex.seen:old:ward_core: Black, cold, and as heavy as stone many times its size. It lay under a hearthstone in an old house. No tool marks it and no fire touches it.
codex.read:old:ward_core: Set down beside the floor it is the same stuff. It is a ward core, cut the way cores are cut at home. The builder of that house came from a ground where a ward needs one.
codex.seen:old:pot_crystal: A single crystal in the form of the inside of a jar. The clay has been broken off it. It came out of an old chest.
codex.read:old:pot_crystal: It breaks into ordinary crystal. A jar of lees lay where the salt failed and nothing found it, and the lees set hard, jar and all. There is enough in one for a staff head.
codex.seen:old:made_bait: Out of an old chest, a bait made and never laid. The remains in it are sealed in matter that lasts, and it still brings its animal up.
codex.read:old:made_bait: Two kinds of bait from two kinds of store, both made ahead and both never laid. Whoever stocked these stores hunted at the great stones in the Guide's order, and nobody came back for them.
codex.born:old:made_bait: Lay it on its altar, peopl. The forebears made it for a stone they were lost before they reached, and it works as well as one made today.
codex.sand:old:made_bait: The hunters stopped going. They walked out and burned their pots, and what they had made stayed in the stores.
codex.seen:old:old_bed: Fibre over boards, out of an old house, the same as the bedrolls we make.
codex.read:old:old_bed: Lying on it moves where a fall comes out, as with our own. The born have no way and no use for one, and one lies in every old house. Whoever lived in these houses had a way.
codex.born:old:old_bed: Those beds are no use to anyone born. The forebears had peopls working for them, as we do now. They slept on those.
codex.seen:old:recall_stone: Crystal and cut lines round a Hīrak gem, made like a small housing. One came out of a sealed store. Desik and Rehakār sell new ones.
codex.read:old:recall_stone: Driven, it puts the bearer at the bed, awake, with nothing shed. It is warm after and will not work until it cools. It works for us and for nobody born.
codex.born:old:recall_stone: I cut new ones line for line from the old. In my hand it does nothing. It works on whatever a peopl is.
codex.seen:old:token: A grey piece of glass with ash in it. It smells of nothing. Sand-country fighters carry them, and the Deserter takes them.
codex.read:old:token: It charges no pot. The Deserter sells for tokens and nothing else, and what he sells came off marches. To his people a token must buy something at a fire.
codex.sand:old:token: Show it at a fire and you sleep inside the light and eat. A marcher carries some in case the walk home runs past dusk.
codex.seen:ground:floor: At the bottom of every shaft we dig is the same black face. No pick marks it. We have taken it for a rock harder than any we know.
codex.read:ground:floor: Wood of the kind cores are cut from is black and cold and takes no mark. So is this. The floor is dead wood, it seems, and more of it in one piece than any of us has seen.
codex.seen:ground:set: A block set in the air stays there with nothing under it. Earth, sand and stone all stay as they are put.
codex.read:ground:set: Cut a tree at the foot and the rest hangs. At home, ground is held that steady only over a ward core. Something under this country holds all of it the way a core holds the ground over it.
codex.seen:ground:way: Gone from where it fell, a failing body comes to at the last bed it lay on, hurt, hungry and short of lees. A bed in the hollow or on the islands marks nothing.
codex.read:ground:way: A recall stone does on purpose what a fall does, without the shedding. So the way each of us came up by is still open behind us, and a body that lets go drops into it.
codex.born:ground:way: A peopl who goes down gets up at its bed. Lie down where you want to get up. We look for you back by morning.
codex.sand:ground:way: Kill a peopl and nobody sees it go. In the morning it is back at the stores. That is why we class you with what a store draws.
codex.seen:ground:light: Nothing comes up where a torch or a lamp throws its light. In the dark, at night or under rock, feeders are found where nothing was.
codex.read:ground:light: A Tama came up in the dark and walked into the torchlight. Light stops them coming up in a place, it seems, and does nothing to one already up.
codex.seen:ground:moon: The moon rises as the sun sets and sets as it rises. A round dark lies across its face, and moves from night to night.
codex.read:ground:moon: On the night the moon was wholly dark, Chandasāvak came up everywhere and the sky took their colour. At dawn the sun took apart every one still standing. They bear no light, it seems, even the moon's.
codex.born:ground:moon: On the dark night the moon is hollow, and what was in it can come down. I tell every peopl which night it falls. That night, be inside walls with a lamp, or out where you mean to fight.
codex.seen:ground:ward: A pot of lees and one hand on a slab of cut stone, all night. No core. While the hand is there, nothing comes up near the house.
codex.read:ground:ward: At dusk the packs walked in past the held room. A charge turns only what is weaker than the kill in it, and two held hearths draw, so a pack led by something stronger crosses.
codex.born:ground:ward: A pot and a hand, peopl. That is a hearth. I sit at it from dusk to first light. Your own bed is no hearth, because nobody holds at it.
codex.sand:ground:ward: A pot is a store, and stores draw. A hand on it draws more. A house with a pot in it is what the dark comes up for.
codex.seen:ground:hosts: Since the first great kill, everything that comes up hits harder and takes more killing. At dusk, packs go for the houses.
codex.read:ground:hosts: It happened again with the second kind. Among feeders a kill is eaten and the eater followed. We boil ours down, so nothing is followed, and the host breaks into packs that feed and grow.
codex.born:ground:hosts: Each great one was set over its country by the forebears when they raised the stones. Kill it and that country is taken back. Kill them all and the stones can be lit again.
codex.sand:ground:hosts: A great one that nothing hunts holds its country. Ours let nothing else come up on the sand. Kill one and its kind run loose, and they go where things are stored.
codex.seen:ground:mouth: Each of us came up on this same low, dry, open ground, alone and with nothing. A fall with no bed laid ends here as well. Nothing is built on it.
codex.read:ground:mouth: Dug down, it is the same floor as anywhere, with no hole in it. The road we came by meets the floor here, and only a pathfinder could step back down into it. None of us is one.
codex.born:ground:mouth: That is where the ground puts out peopls, with nothing in their hands. None of us sleeps on it or digs there.
